headers.description: Optional headers to send with the request as a dictionary of header values.

Content-Type.description: The media type of the resource being requested, typically 'application/json'.

Authorization.description: The credentials to authenticate a user agent with a server, typically formatted as 'Bearer {token}'.

timeout.description: The maximum amount of time to wait for a response from the server, in seconds. A longer timeout may be necessary for slower network connections or overloaded servers. This is a float type value.

params.description: URL parameters to append to the URL. Sent as a dictionary of key-value pairs.

query.description: The query parameter for search or filtering.

page.description: The page number parameter for pagination. Used to retrieve a specific page of results.

auth.description: HTTP authentication credentials formatted as a tuple of strings (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem), if required for the request.

cookies.description: Cookies to send with the request as a dictionary of cookie names and values.

sessionid.description: Session identifier cookie, used to recognize client sessions on the server.

csrftoken.description: CSRF protection token cookie, used to prevent cross-site request forgery attacks.

proxies.description: Proxy settings as a dictionary, mapping protocol or protocol and hostname to the URL of the proxy.

http.description: Proxy URL to use for HTTP requests, including the port number.

https.description: Proxy URL to use for HTTPS requests, including the port number.

stream.description: Whether to stream the download of the response. If False, the response content will be immediately downloaded. Streaming is useful for handling large files or responses.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not. Set to False to skip certificate verification, which is not recommended unless you are sure of the server's identity.

Sure! Finding a short‑running film right next to Times Square is pretty easy once you know where to look. Here’s a quick playbook: | Step | What to do | Why it helps | |------|------------|--------------| | **1️⃣ Pick a nearby theater** | • **AMC Empire 25** – 25 screens, 12‑hour schedule, located at 234 W 42nd St (just a 5‑min walk).
• **Regal Union Square** – 10 screens, 13‑hour schedule, about a 7‑min walk.
• **Alamo Drafthouse** – 8 screens, 15‑hour schedule, ~10‑min walk. | These are the biggest chains in the area, so they’ll have the widest selection of titles and showtimes. | | **2️⃣ Check the official website or app** | • Go to the theater’s site (e.g., `www.amctheatres.com` or `www.regmovies.com`).
• Enter “Times Square” or your exact address into the “Find a Theater” field.
• Browse the “Now Showing” list. | The sites list each film’s runtime next to the title, plus the exact start times. | | **3️⃣ Filter by runtime** | • On AMC’s site, click the “Showtime Filters” button → tick “≤ 120 min”.
• On Regal’s site, use the “Runtime” slider to set max 120 min.
• Alamo has a “Short Films” section for under‑2‑hour features. | You’ll instantly see only those films that meet your length requirement. | | **4️⃣ Verify the showtime window** | • Look for a screening that starts after your free time and ends before you need to leave.
• Add the film’s start time + runtime + 30 min buffer (for travel & snacks). | Makes sure you’re not stuck waiting for a late‑night ending. | | **5️⃣ Book tickets in advance** | • Buy online through the theater’s site or a ticket aggregator (Fandango, Atom Tickets).
• Choose a seat in the middle row for optimal viewing. | Saves you a queue at the box office and guarantees a seat. | ### Quick “one‑click” options If you prefer a single step, try this: ```text https://www.fandango.com/search?q=Times+Square+NYC&filters=runtime%3A120 ``` This link (replace `fandango.com` with your local domain if needed) pulls up all movies showing in NYC theaters within 120 minutes. Just scroll to the “Near Me” section and pick a theater close to Times Square. --- #### Bonus tip: Use IMDb Advanced Search If you’d rather browse titles first, head to IMDb’s advanced search: ```text https://www.imdb.com/search/title/?title_type=feature&release_date=2023-01-01,2023-12-31&runtime=80,120&sort=user_rating,desc ``` Replace the year range with the current year. Once you’ve chosen a film, copy its title into the theater’s search bar to see if it’s playing now. Happy watching! Let me know if you’d like help picking a specific film or finding snack deals.
